name: kube-oidc-proxy
description: A reverse proxy that brings OIDC login to managed Kubernetes clusters and accepts tokens from several issuers through one proxy, impersonating the mapped identity against the API server so RBAC stays authoritative.
description_good_justification: The README opens with what the proxy does and why: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy#kube-oidc-proxy
interact_justification: The README links the signed OCI chart and GHCR image for installation, CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/development.md for contributing, the issue tracker for bug reports and SECURITY.md for vulnerabilities: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy#contributing
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the branch model, the test requirement for behaviour changes, the CI gates, the commit style and the changelog-fragment requirement: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
documentation_basics_justification: Getting started, configuration, authentication, operations and security docs under docs/: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the command-line flags, the Helm chart values, the structured log schema and the metrics catalogue; all are documented, the last two generated from code and verified in CI: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/docs/configuration.md, https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/chart/kube-oidc-proxy/README.md, https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/docs/logging.md, https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/docs/metrics.md
sites_https_justification: Project site, repository, GHCR image registry and Artifact Hub listing are all served over HTTPS.
english_justification: All documentation, issues and code comments are in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: regular releases (v1.8.1 is current), weekly Dependabot and vulnerability scans, and a documented maintenance model in MAINTAINING.md: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/releases
repo_track_justification: Git history records every change with author and date; main only accepts pull requests that pass the required unit, lint, vulnerability, CodeQL and e2e checks, with linear history enforced.
repo_interim_justification: Every merged pull request is on main between releases; interim builds are available from the main branch.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique vX.Y.Z tag and a matching CHANGELOG section; the release workflow refuses to retarget an existing tag: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/docs/releases.md
version_semver_justification: Semantic versioning is enforced by the release contract: every PR carries a release/major, release/minor, release/patch or release/skip label and the highest wins: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/docs/releases.md#release-model
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and the GitHub Release for each tag.
release_notes_vulns_justification: CHANGELOG.md names the project's own fixed vulnerability (CVE-2025-68121, fixed in the 1.0.11 line this fork carries: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). docs/releases.md requires every Security fragment to name its advisory so future release notes keep doing so.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting issues' and the issue templates: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-issues
report_responses_justification: Issues from non-maintainers are acknowledged and resolved; see the closed issues list: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed
enhancement_responses_justification: Feature requests use a dedicated template and are answered in the tracker: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting (Security Advisories) is enabled and is the documented channel: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within a few days, well inside 14 days.
build_justification: go build ./... and the Makefile (make build, make verify, make test); the container image is built from the Dockerfile.
build_common_tools_justification: Standard Go toolchain, GNU make and Docker.
build_floss_tools_justification: Go, make, Docker, kind and Helm are all FLOSS.
test_justification: Unit tests under cmd/ and pkg/ (go test) plus a Kubernetes end-to-end suite on kind run as three shards in CI: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yaml and e2e.yaml
test_invocation_justification: go test ./cmd/... ./pkg/... for unit tests and make e2e for the end-to-end suite, as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.
test_most_justification: No coverage service is wired up yet; coverage is not measured in CI.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs build, vet, gofmt, lint, unit tests, Helm checks, govulncheck and CodeQL on every pull request and push to main. The Kubernetes end-to-end shards run on every pull request, twice daily on a schedule against main, and again inside the release workflow before a tag is created.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: 'include tests for behaviour changes', and the release workflow only tags a commit that passed unit and e2e checks: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests
tests_are_added_justification: Feature pull requests land with tests; for example the metrics (#155, #156) and multi-issuer Secret (#163, #164) changes each add unit, contract and e2e coverage.
warnings_justification: go vet (both build-tag configurations), gofmt and golangci-lint with errcheck, staticcheck, gosec, revive, bodyclose and the default analysers gate every pull request: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/.golangci.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: golangci-lint run ./... reports 0 issues on the whole repository, and go vet and gofmt are clean; CI fails a pull request on any new finding.
warnings_strict_justification: staticcheck runs with checks: all, gosec is enabled and every suppression must carry a reason (.golangci.yml).
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designed the authentication path with least privilege: the proxy validates tokens fail-closed, authorizes any client-requested impersonation with a SubjectAccessReview before honouring it, and leaves authorization of the Kubernetes API operation itself to the API server's RBAC for the mapped identity. Label and event sets are closed so clients cannot grow metric or log cardinality, and the threat scope is documented in SECURITY.md and docs/architecture.md.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25 classes relevant to an authentication proxy (injection, broken authentication, SSRF, header smuggling, log injection); the codebase addresses them with strict token parsing, trusted-proxy allow-lists for client IP, printable-ASCII bounds on inbound request ids, and gosec plus CodeQL in CI.
crypto_published_justification: Only published algorithms are used: TLS from the Go standard library and JOSE/JWT signature verification via go-oidc and the Kubernetes apiserver authentication libraries.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptography is implemented in this project; all of it is called from the Go standard library and the Kubernetes and go-oidc libraries.
crypto_floss_justification: Go standard library crypto, go-oidc and k8s.io/apiserver are all FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: Key lengths are those of the Go TLS defaults and of the issuer's JWKS keys; the proxy generates no long-term keys of its own.
crypto_working_justification: Go's TLS stack and go-oidc reject broken algorithms; no MD5, DES or RC4 is used anywhere in the project.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The Go TLS server defaults (TLS 1.2 minimum, no RC4, no CBC on TLS 1.3) are used unchanged; JWT 'none' and symmetric algorithms are rejected by the token verifier.
crypto_pfs_justification: Go's default TLS cipher suite preference uses ECDHE key exchange, so every TLS session has forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The proxy stores no passwords or user credentials; authentication is by bearer token verified against the issuer's published keys.
crypto_random_justification: All randomness comes from the Go standard library's crypto/rand: TLS session material via the TLS stack, and the per-process 32-byte HMAC key the TokenReview cache draws with rand.Read to key token hashes (pkg/proxy/tokenreview/tokenreview.go).
delivery_mitm_justification: Source, the container image (ghcr.io) and the OCI Helm chart are all delivered over HTTPS; image and chart are signed with cosign keyless signatures and the image carries an SBOM: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-image.yaml
delivery_unsigned_justification: cosign signatures for the image and chart are published to the same registry over HTTPS, never over an insecure channel.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Dependency advisories are surfaced weekly by Dependabot and govulncheck and fixed in the next release; the open Dependabot advisories are all under 60 days old with update PRs already open, and govulncheck confirms none is reachable from this code (see the Security entries in CHANGELOG.md).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical advisories are fixed promptly: CVE-2025-68121 was fixed in the upstream 1.0.11 line that this fork carries, and GO-2026-6094 / GO-2026-6107 were remediated in 1.8.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed to the repository. CI authenticates with short-lived OIDC tokens (id-token: write) and the ephemeral GITHUB_TOKEN; the two long-lived secrets it uses (a release-approval PAT and the Claude review token) are held as GitHub Actions encrypted secrets, referenced only via secrets.* in workflows, and the e2e suite mints its own test tokens at run time.
static_analysis_justification: GitHub CodeQL on every pull request, push and weekly; golangci-lint (staticcheck, gosec, errcheck, revive) on every pull request: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security queries and gosec both target common weakness classes.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open findings; the only open code-scanning items are Scorecard posture notes, which SECURITY.md documents as accepted.
static_analysis_often_justification: Runs on every pull request, every push to main and on a weekly schedule.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Go native fuzzing of the parsers that take attacker-controlled input (bearer token extraction, trusted-proxy CIDR parsing, flag parsing) runs weekly with the seed corpora exercised on every pull request: https://github.com/RafPe/kube-oidc-proxy/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yaml. The Kubernetes end-to-end suite exercises the running proxy on kind on every pull request.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Go is memory-safe, but the race detector (go test -race) is not yet part of CI; enabling it is tracked, since a local run surfaces a race inside the client-go certificate-rotation helper that the tests drive directly.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests compile with -tags logcheck, which enables the required-attribute assertions inside the logging layer so a record missing a mandatory field fails a test instead of shipping.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The fuzz workflow uploads any failing input as an artifact so it can be committed as a regression seed under testdata/fuzz; there are no open fuzz or e2e findings.
